insights.content: Wiki: codespace-playbook.md — Comprehensive guide for GitHub operations in Codespaces. Covers token extraction from VS Code server (/proc/PID/environ), gh CLI setup, PR monitoring, git push, common pitfalls. Read wiki/codespace-playbook.md for full details.

Wiki: repository-analysis.md — Deep dive of hermes-codespace architecture. Covers startup flow (install.sh → boot.sh → Hermes Agent), what's used vs unused, self-check.sh validation, CI verification. Read wiki/repository-analysis.md for full details.

Wiki: github-actions-testing-plan.md — Phased CI/CD testing plan for hermes-codespace. Covers path-filtered CI with dorny/paths-filter@v3, lint checks (markdownlint, SKILL.md validation, shell syntax), full build with pre-build and smoke test. Read wiki/github-actions-testing-plan.md for full details.

Wiki: persistent-knowledge-proposal.md — Architecture decision document for the Persistent Knowledge System. Covers symlink-based skills persistence, wiki base, Mnemon seeding, directory structure, boot workflow. Read wiki/persistent-knowledge-proposal.md for full details.

GITHUB_TOKEN extraction: The real GITHUB_TOKEN is in the VS Code server's process environment at /proc/<PID>/environ, NOT in the shell env. GITHUB_CODESPACE_TOKEN in shell is useless for API calls. GH_TOKEN is set to an invalid value. See wiki/codespace-playbook.md section 2 for details.

Persistent Knowledge System uses symlinks (not rsync/cp). ~/.hermes/skills/codespace → skills/. Writes to the symlinked path land directly in the workspace. Git sees everything. Boot script: boot.sh creates symlink on every start (idempotent, checks first).

Boot script location: boot.sh (NOT install.sh). boot.sh runs on every Codespace start/rebuild, making it the reliable place for idempotent setup like symlink creation and Mnemon seeding. install.sh only runs on first create.

Path-filtered CI: ci.yml uses dorny/paths-filter@v3 with three jobs. detect-changes classifies files into infrastructure/runtime/docs. full-build runs only for infrastructure changes (~15min). lint-check runs for docs/runtime changes (~30s). Concurrency group cancels in-progress runs.

Hermes discovers skills via os.walk(followlinks=True) with ~30s cache TTL. New skills written to ~/.hermes/skills/codespace/ (symlinked to skills/) are auto-discovered within ~30 seconds. No restart needed. Skill format: SKILL.md with YAML frontmatter (name, description, version).

Mnemon is the persistent memory system for Hermes. CLI: mnemon remember/recall/search/import. Database at ~/.mnemon/data/default/mnemon.db. Import format: JSON with schema_version '1' and insights array. Deduplication built-in. Categories: preference, decision, insight, fact, context. Importance: 1-5.

CI Fix: Silent failures from npm ci. When npm ci fails, it kills the process before writing error output. Fix: pre-build web UI in install.sh using 'npm ci CI=1 --include=dev --workspace web' with explicit error handling and fallback to 'npm install'. See install.sh for the pattern.

CI Debugging lesson: Fix root cause, never weaken the test. Silent failures are hardest — when a process is killed before writing output, you get zero error info. Always compare passing vs failing commits to find the real cause. Self-check.sh CRITICAL_SERVICES variable is defined but unused — all services are always critical.

Wiki naming convention: Use 'wiki' (not 'knowledge' or 'KNOWLEDGE.md'). Follows LM Wiki / Karpathy concept of interlinked markdown articles. .hermes.md instructs agent to read from wiki/. INDEX.md serves as table of contents.

Knowledge capture workflow: Both proactive AND user-triggered. Agent proposes entries for seed.json (importance >= 4 or new wiki/skill). User reviews via git diff, approves/rejects, commits when ready. Same pattern as skills: agent proposes, user reviews, git persists.

HARD RULE: Before merging ANY PR, always check GitHub CodeQL and Copilot review suggestions (if available). Use the github-pr-review skill to fetch, triage, and evaluate comments. Present findings to user for approval before merging. This is a merge gate — do not skip.

Mnemon seed import in boot.sh uses dry-run validation first, then real import. Output parsing must use 'imported' field (not 'added') — the mnemon import JSON returns {imported, skipped, updated, errors}. Fixed grep pattern to match actual output format.

Refactored boot.sh with unified dependency validation: single loop checks 5 binaries (9router, omniroute, ollama, hermes, mnemon) + skills directory + seed.json. Fails fast with FATAL message listing all missing items. Simplified service sections to use pgrep only.

github-pr-review skill: 5-step workflow for evaluating GitHub CodeQL and Copilot suggestions on PRs. Fetch comments, triage by source, evaluate (ACCEPT/REJECT/DEFER), present proposal as table, implement after approval. Decision framework: always accept security findings, reject false positives, defer architectural changes.

Keepalive implementation: keepalive.sh service started by boot.sh to prevent idle shutdown. Contains A+B approach: (A) periodic terminal heartbeat on hermes's pty to mimic user activity (GitHub platform idle detection), (B) internal pinger hitting VS Code server /delay-shutdown endpoint to reset server-side shutdown timer (5-min grace). Testable with --test flag. Wires into container lifecycle, idempotent, survives start/rebuild.

Persistent Memory Option A (validated 2026-08): install.sh is authoritative for symlink creation (runs once on fresh container, right after Hermes install, before Hermes instantiates ~/.hermes/memories). boot.sh keeps only a slim repair guard (~12 lines) for pre-existing containers where postCreateCommand doesn't re-run. Symlink: ~/.hermes/memories → memories/ (whole folder, skills pattern). .gitignore in tracked dir ignores *.lock *.log. Mnemon primary rule preserved in tracked USER.md.

Self-check.sh Persistence section (section 9) validates both memories and skills symlinks: 9a) ~/.hermes/memories → memories, 9b) ~/.hermes/skills/codespace → skills. Each handles 3 cases: correct symlink (ok), real dir (fail), missing (fail). 9c (tracked content existence) removed as redundant with git checkout. CI lint-check also validates symlinks via standalone step for runtime changes.

CI path-filter for persistence: memories/** and skills/** are in runtime (not infrastructure) so content changes trigger 30s lint-check, not 15min full-build. lint-check now includes 'Validate symlink persistence' step asserting both symlinks. infrastructure remains boot scripts only (install.sh, boot.sh, self-check.sh, devcontainer.json, workflows). This keeps CI fast for content edits while still gating symlink correctness.

Wiki: persistent-memory-proposal.md — Architecture decision document for Hermes persistent memory (MEMORY.md/USER.md) versioning via whole-folder symlink. Covers Option A split (install authoritative + start-hermes guard), self-check validation, CI wiring, .gitignore for lock/log files, Mnemon primary rule in USER.md. Read wiki/persistent-memory-proposal.md for full details.

Skill: codespace-persistent-symlinks — Procedural skill for persisting Hermes state (memories + skills) across Codespace rebuilds via whole-folder symlinks. Documents Option A placement, self-check verification, 3-case guard logic, pitfalls (seed block removal, head truncation bug, verification cases). Symlink pattern mirrors skills: ~/.hermes/memories → memories/, ~/.hermes/skills/codespace → skills/. Read skills-persistent-symlinks/SKILL.md for full procedure.
HARD RULE: Never commit or push directly to main. All changes to main must go through a pull request (branch -> push -> PR -> review -> merge). User explicitly mandated this.

HARD RULE: For ANY coding task (writing, editing, reviewing, refactoring, debugging code), always load the karpathy-coding-guidelines skill first (skill_view) and follow its discipline. User explicitly mandated this. The skill itself exempts trivial one-liners from full rigor.

codespace-port-visibility skill scripts location: ~/.hermes/skills/codespace/codespace-port-visibility/scripts/ (get_codespace_token.py, set_port_visibility.py, export_codespace_token.sh). Symlinked to skills-port-visibility/scripts/ for persistence.

Skill: codespace-vscode-open — Auto-discovers VS Code CLI in Codespaces at /vscode/bin/linux-x64/<commit>/bin/remote-cli/code and opens files in connected VS Code. Script at ~/.hermes/scripts/vscode-open.sh and skills-vscode-open/scripts/vscode-open.sh. Wiki: wiki/vscode-cli-codespaces.md. Use this skill whenever you need to open a file in the user's VS Code from a Codespace.

MANDATORY: Run ci-lint-check skill before ANY commit or PR that modifies skills/**, wiki/**, mnemon/**, memories/**, or *.sh. This mirrors the GitHub Actions lint-check job and prevents CI failures. One command: bash skills/ci-lint-check/scripts/ci_lint_check.sh

codespace-lavish skill fully installed and working: launches headed Lavish-AXI whiteboard over noVNC with auto-connect (autoconnect=true) and local scaling (resize=scale). Includes continuous poll loop with auto-restart (2s), --monitor flag, Chrome GPU fix (SwiftShader), session key derivation, and stable noVNC URL. Script is idempotent and self-healing.

When the user asks to launch/start/open a 'webtop', 'remote desktop', 'browser desktop', 'VNC alternative', or 'Selkies/XFCE desktop' in a Codespace or Ubuntu environment, LOAD the codespace-webtop skill and run its control script. The skill lives at skills-webtop/ with scripts/selkies-native.sh (install/start/stop/status/autostart/logs). Quick path: bash skills-webtop/scripts/selkies-native.sh start, then forward port 3000. CRITICAL: use the pixelflux-based selkies wheel (GitHub Actions 'selkies-wheel' artifact), NOT PyPI selkies==1.6.1 (legacy GStreamer). Requires libva2 libva-drm2 libva-x11-2 for H.264.

Skill: mnemon-graph-export — Export Mnemon knowledge graph to 3D viewer. Location: skills/mnemon-graph-export/. Trigger: "export mnemon graph", "regenerate knowledge graph", "update 3D viewer", "new graph from mnemon". Usage: cd skills/mnemon-graph-export/scripts && python3 export_graph.py (fresh graph.json + graph-data.js) && python3 -m http.server 8130 (serve viewer at localhost:8130 or file:// mnemon-graph.html). Viewer loads data at runtime — data refresh never needs rebuild; only template.html changes require python3 build.py (vendors 3d-force-graph@1.80 with SRI pin). Wiki: wiki/mnemon-graph-viewer.md.

docker-test-shell skill at skills/docker-test-shell/ provides the `dts` primitive for testing any tool in a clean throwaway ubuntu:24.04 container. Key commands: `dts up` (fresh container, repo at /src, uid-1000), `dts exec "<cmd>"` (run as uid-1000, bash -l, -i no -t), `dts apt "<pkgs>"` (root apt installs), `dts shell` (interactive -it), `dts clean` (remove container), `dts status` (state). Verified end-to-end with OmniRoute 3.8.50: dts up -> dts apt xz-utils g++ make -> dts exec install.sh -> dts exec hermes chat -q works via auto-fastest combo. Golden rules: never trust host, -i not -it when scripted, bash -l login shell, uid-1000 parity, apt via dts apt not exec, md5 verify mount, always dts clean. Root vs uid-1000: test commands always uid-1000 (CI parity); root only for apt (dts apt) or explicit inspection (docker exec -u 0:0).

HARD RULE: Always use the repo's `tdd` skill (skills/tdd) for test-driven development — NEVER the stock Hermes `test-driven-development` skill. The repo tdd skill is the Hermes-adapted superpowers version + mattpocock's seam-confirmation and tautological-test checks, persisted and versioned. It is the single source of truth for TDD.

Skill: grill-with-docs (skills/grill-with-docs + references/CONTEXT-FORMAT.md + references/ADR-FORMAT.md). Merges mattpocock's grill-with-docs and domain-modeling. Behavior: relentless interview to sharpen a plan/design while writing a domain glossary (CONTEXT.md) and ADRs as we go. Sections: interview mode, challenge against glossary, sharpen fuzzy language, edge-case scenarios, cross-reference code, update CONTEXT.md inline, offer ADRs sparingly. CONTEXT.md is a glossary and nothing else; an ADR needs ALL of: hard to reverse, surprising without context, real trade-off.

The stock Hermes `test-driven-development` skill (~/.hermes/skills/software-development/) is superseded by the repo `tdd` skill. Do not load or prefer it; use tdd. It is not git-tracked and is an obsolete copy (kept for now, not deleted).
